name: FL-06
label: Likely R

key_factors: Fine's large financial advantage ($4.3M raised, $3.7M outside support)
Markets price Fine near 95% to win
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The R+14 district, incumbent Randy Fine's overwhelming fundraising edge, and prediction markets pricing him around 95% all point to a comfortable Republican hold. Democrat Eric Yonce's modest fundraising gives little evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Fine underperforming the district's lean, or a surge of outside spending against him, would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican incumbent Randy Fine seeks a second full term in this heavily Republican Florida district, where the partisan lean favors his party by roughly fourteen points. He enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised over $4 million and benefited from more than $3.7 million in outside support, while holding over $1 million on hand.

Democratic challenger Eric Yonce has raised about $326,000, a fraction of the incumbent's total, and no independent or minor-party candidate appears positioned to alter the race. No public polls are available, but prediction markets give Fine roughly a 95 percent chance of winning. The fundamentals and money advantage point to a safe Republican hold, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
